script.opening_words: Ruth retired at 64 with $410,000. She died at 79 with $437,000. 15 years. 15 winters with the thermostat at 66 because the furnace was original to the house and she never found out what

claim_audit: Ruth, Jean/Gene, Denise and Curtis are illustrative, not identified longitudinal households. Ruth starting $410K and ending $437K is a $27K nominal increase, not proof she spent nothing or that real assets grew: at analyst-assumed 2.5% inflation for15years, $437K equals about $301,733 in initial dollars. Returns, pensions/benefits, withdrawals, taxes, debts and bequests are absent. An unbooked trip and thermostat vignette cannot establish optimal spending or the modal retiree outcome.

EBRI2018 primary summary supports median11.8%asset decline over20years among retirees starting500K+, and roughly one-third growing assets. It does not say everyone died holding88%, identify gross lifetime consumption, or imply an unspent principal equals forgone enjoyment. Balance change includes returns and cash flows; income can fund consumption without decumulation. Median cohort outcomes are not every viewer future. Survivor/attrition and original sample/asset definitions matter; only primary summary checked, not a reanalysis of microdata.

EBRI pension comparison explicitly says pensioners STARTED WITH MUCH HIGHER ASSETS; script says holding the same money and only income shape differs. Four versus34%median non-housing decline over18years is observational and confounded by pension income, startingwealth, household and other characteristics. It does not identify pensions as the sole causal permission mechanism. Pension benefits also depend on plan, survivor options, inflation protection and counterparty/guarantee arrangements; not every pension is an unlimited riskless check.

4%of600K=24K plus45KSocialSecurity=69K;3.5%=21K and total66K, before account-specific taxes. Changing3.5%to5% frees9Kinitialannual, NOT18K. Expert3.3%-5.5%range on600K spans13.2K, NOT20K. Compounding/declining-balance future paths require separate assumptions. Choosing a lower rate can still have failure risk; lowest cannot get you in trouble is false. Bengen historical versus Morningstar forward-looking methods and horizons are not interchangeable expert opinions to average.

Morningstar2025 base case3.9%initial/30years/90%modeledsuccess is conditional on allocation/assumptions; not a universal target or guarantee. Fivepercentplus may need flexible spending, different horizon or risk. Savings are not all fun money once a present income floor covers present bills: care, longevity, maintenance, taxes, survivor changes and inflation/benefit risk remain. No floor/expense ledger shows delaying both spouses actually covers costs permanently.

RMD600K/26.5=$22,641.51 and3.7736% reproduce for a qualifying age73uniform-table case, using prior-year-end balance, not automatically the same original600K at65. RMD requires distribution, NOT consumption: after-tax proceeds can be reinvested in a taxable account. RothIRAs/designatedRoth owner rules differ. Starting age depends on birth cohort, with age75for later cohorts, plus applicable workplace deferral/ownership rules. Retiring64to79doesnot produce15age73RMDs; Ruth15minimums lacks a coherent account/tax-law timeline. Rates at73and65 applied to one fixed balance are not actual observed cash flow.

Allianz67%fear-versus-death,57%in2022, pensioncoverage38%/midteens,43%near-retirement noaccounts,half dyingunder10K, typical inheritanceage58/30%everinherit and tenchannel-success promotion lack matched original sources here. A fear response is not literal preference to die. Losses twice gains is a context-dependent behavioral generalization, not a universal response coefficient. An adult58with a house can still value/need20K; age doesnot establish wealth, obligations or utility.

Genworth/CareScout latest2025survey, releasedMarch2,2026, reports assistedliving74,400annual and private nursing129,575, versus narrated roughly70K/127K closer to older data. Local costs/provider needs vary. Fidelity July2025single65yearoldestimate172,500 and April2026couple345K after-tax estimate excludingLTC support the couple number, with eligibility/longevity/model assumptions—not a universal bill. A separate institutional PDF search excerpt ambiguously labels345Ksingle; primary consumer page and2025release resolve unit rather than silently choosing the snippet.

OriginalMedicare generally excludes nonmedical custodial long-termcare and routine dental/hearing/vision categories, but approximately none of teeth/eyes/ears is too broad: medically linked dental exceptions, covered eye/medical services and someMedicareAdvantage extras differ. Skilled medically necessary care is not the same as long-termcustodial care. LTCinsurer counts, age70denials50% and reliableinsurability require dated product/underwriting samples; not all older people face the same offer.

About70%anyLTC need is not equivalent to5years paidcare. The exact4%-5%five-year-paidcare claim requires a matched severe-disability/formalcare cohort, horizon and person-versus-household denominator; retrievedASPE references distinguish these but do not independently substantiate that exact comparison. ACL/ASPE direct pages hit403, so no full source review claimed. Jean/Denise TWO-person household chance cannot silently equal one-person rate, and tail severity/preferences matter even at low probability. Reserving300K is not inherently irrational without household risk, assets and benefit options.

JPMorgan75Kage60-64versus52Kage90-94 is an unverified exact table here. Cross-sectional age spending is not automatically the same household trajectory, and death/health/householdsize/cohort/asset selection affect comparisons.75to52is30.7%decline arithmetically, but the text switches endpoint to85. Lower average spending does not establish every future dollar has lower value or that current5%withdrawals are safe.

SSA2026Trustees supports projected OASIreserve depletionQ42032; ongoing income could pay78%scheduledbenefits at depletion under its assumptions. CombinedOASDIprojection2034is separate; retirementfund runningdry doesnot mean all benefits cease. These are current-law projections, not a certain outcome. DelayingSocialSecurityto70 can increase benefits and hedge longevity, but bestannuityfor everyone ignores health, liquidity, spouse/survivor, tax and benefit-legislation risk. BeforeFRAreductions and afterFRA8%delayedcredits differ; a universal7%peryearfrom62is not the actual formula.

Spending portfolio from65to70 DOES deplete assets absent offsettingreturns, even if exchanging liquidity for later income can be rational. Must compare forgone checks, bridgecost, expectedlifetimes and survivorbenefits. Dividend400versusselling400 can be economically similar beforetax around ex-dividend price adjustment, but taxes/account/basis/transaction timing differ; principal and income are not guaranteed interchangeable aftertax.

PreRMDyears can offer Rothconversion opportunities but are not automatically cheapest: taxableconversion amount, bracket, otherincome, Medicarepremium/ACA interactions and futuretaxes matter. RMDitself is not eligible for rollover/conversion; annualage/birthcohort rules apply. Gift20Kfromonepersontoonerecipient in2026exceeds19Kannualexclusion and generally may requireForm709, though not automatically taxdue; spouses/exclusions/othergift rules can change treatment. Estate/bequest goals and lifeexpectancy are preferences, not failed spending. Disclaimers do not validate universal never-spend and safety claims.
